title: Bram and the Glitter Hiccups
markdown:
Once upon a time, in a cozy spot amongst the soft clouds and sweet flowers, lived a little goblin named Bram. Bram was a very happy little fellow, with a nose that wiggled and jiggled like a happy jellybean. And his green boots! They were the brightest green you ever did see, like new leaves after a gentle rain. Bram loved his home in the Cloudpetal Mountains. The soft moss felt like velvet under his feet, and the air was always filled with the soft, quiet hum of sleepy bumblebees drifting from one flower to the next.

Every single day, Bram would walk along the sleepy cedar trail. This trail was special, you see. The trees stood tall and quiet. Their needles smelled like a warm, sunny afternoon. They smelled a little like cookies baking, too! As Bram skipped along, he would hum a little goblin hum. It was a tune as light and airy as a dandelion puff. And, as if they could hear his happy song, the little pebbles on the path would skip and bounce beside him. It was as though they were dancing to his happy tune. Skip, skip, hop! they seemed to say.

But one day, as Bram hummed his happy tune, a funny sound tickled his ears. Hic! It wasn't the sound of a bumblebee buzzing. It wasn't a pebble skipping. No, this was a tiny, tinkly sound, like little bells jingling. Bram’s wiggliest nose twitched. He was curious! He tiptoed, his green boots making soft thuds on the moss. He peeked behind a big, round mushroom. It was fat and soft, like a cushion. And what did he see? Oh, something amazing, truly!

It was a baby dragon! But now, don’t you worry your sweet head. This wasn’t a fire-breathing, roary sort of dragon at all. Oh, goodness no. This little dragon was no bigger than Bram’s smoothest pebble. Its scales were the soft, lovely color of a clear summer sky. A perfect blue! And its eyes, my dear, were like two shiny, bright blueberries. And here’s the truly wondrous part: every time it gave a tiny Hic!, out puffed a little ring of glittery, rainbow-colored smoke! It floated in the air for a moment, shimmering, then disappeared like a happy sigh.

"Oh, my goodness gracious!" Bram whispered. His wiggliest nose twitched even faster with wonder.

The baby dragon looked up at Bram, its big blueberry eyes blinking. Hic! And out puffed another small ring of sparkling, rainbow glitter.

"Hello there," Bram said. His voice was as soft and gentle as a whispered lullaby. "Are you feeling quite alright, little one?"

The baby dragon gave a tiny shake of its little head. Then, as if to answer, Hic! Another shimmering ring of glitter puffed out into the soft mountain air.

"Oh, you have the hiccups!" Bram giggled. It was a soft, bubbly sound, like tiny dewdrop bells. "That reminds me of my Auntie Griselda. She gets them sometimes, and she shakes and wobbles like a teacup on a shaky shelf!"

The little dragon blinked again. Its blueberry eyes were wide. Hic! A small ring of pink glitter floated past Bram’s nose.

Because of those glittery hiccups, Bram’s kind heart knew he simply had to help his new, sparkly-hiccuping friend.

Bram thought very hard. He tapped his chin with a little green finger. He remembered what his wise Auntie Griselda always said about stopping hiccups. "You must either have a very big drink of cool water," she’d explained, her voice like rustling leaves, "or you must tell a very, very funny story!"

"Hmm," Bram hummed. He looked around the gentle path. "There isn't any water to be found on this sleepy cedar trail right now. But a funny story… I do know a funny story!" A little spark lit up in his bright goblin eyes.

Because of that, Bram found the softest patch of moss by the trail and sat down. He made sure his bright green boots were planted perfectly still, like little green garden gnomes. "Once upon a time," he began. His voice was as soft as the gentle rustle of leaves in a summer breeze. "There was a grumpy old badger. And this badger, oh my, he wore spectacles that were far, far too big for his nose. They kept slipping down! And because they were so big, he kept bumping right into the trees!" Bram watched the little dragon. It was watching him with its blueberry eyes wide. Hic! A small ring of pink and orange glitter puffed out.

"And then!" Bram continued. His voice got a little more excited. "The grumpy badger tried to eat a juicy worm, but he made a mistake! He accidentally ate his own fuzzy slipper instead! And he said, in his grumbly voice, 'Oh dear me, this worm is uncommonly… leathery!'"

At this, the little dragon let out a tiny, happy squeak. It sounded like a delicate chime. Hic! A ring of bright blue and sunny gold glitter puffed out. This one was even bigger than the last.

Bram couldn't help but let out a little chuckle. It was a warm, happy sound. "And wouldn’t you know it," he said. His voice was now full of pure glee. "The badger’s big spectacles fell right off his nose and plopped into a muddy puddle! He couldn't see a single thing, not one little bit, and he waddled around the forest like a lost duck, quacking to himself!"

And at that, my dear child, the little dragon gave a huge, rumbling giggle. It sounded like a cascade of tiny pebbles rolling happily down a gentle hill. Hic! But this time, no glitter puff came out at all. Instead, a big, beautiful rainbow of sparkles burst into the air. It shimmered and swirled and twirled in a wonderful display. Then came another giggle, and another. And with each joyful sound, the hiccups just… vanished!

The little dragon looked up at Bram. Its blueberry eyes were shining with pure happiness. It nuzzled Bram’s bright green boot with its tiny, scaly nose. It was a gesture of perfect friendship.

"You're all better!" Bram exclaimed. He clapped his hands together softly. "My funny story was just the thing you needed!"

The little dragon seemed to nod its head. Then it gave a soft, sleepy sigh. It curled up on the wonderfully soft moss. Its sky-blue scales sparkled like little gems in the dappled sunlight filtering through the cedar trees.

Now, you see, that's the curious thing about a good story. It can do all sorts of truly wonderful things, like stopping hiccups and making new friends.

Bram watched his new friend sleep. The sleepy cedar trail was quiet and peaceful once more. He knew, deep in his goblin heart, that he would never, ever forget the little dragon who hiccuped glitter.

And ever since that delightful day, whenever Bram heard a tiny hic, he would smile. It was a big, happy smile that reached all the way to his wiggliest nose. He would remember the day he helped a baby dragon. And how a silly story had painted the sky with glittery rainbows.

That’s how Bram, the little goblin with the wiggliest nose and the brightest green boots, made a brand new friend in the quiet and happy Cloudpetal Mountains. And they both had a truly wonderful, glittery adventure indeed.
characters: Bram the young goblin, a little dragon
